fields.m.setting: Self-contained ESE classroom, 8 students, 1 teacher, 2 paraprofessionals
fields.m.beh: Aggression: hitting, kicking or head-butting an adult or peer with enough force to be heard or to move the person; includes attempts blocked by staff. Not: brushing past, tapping to get attention.
fields.m.reinf: Escape from multi-step written work (math worksheets, copying); EO strongest after a transition from preferred play and on days after short sleep.
fields.m.prec: Pushes the worksheet or materials away, says 'no' or 'I'm done', slumps in the chair; within 30 s of the first demand of a work period.
fields.m.repdesc: Says 'break' when prompted; does not use it on his own; a break card is new.
fields.m.pref: PA-1 (MSWO, 9/19): tablet drawing app > Lego bin > bubbles > stickers; social praise mildly effective.
fields.m.curr: Math worksheets are at grade level; Mateo reads at K level, so written directions are not readable to him; copying tasks are long (15 min).
fields.m.constraints: Two paras share eight students; a quiet corner exists; no 1:1 aide.
fields.m.safety: Hits leave marks; no injuries needing a nurse so far; two peers avoid him.
fields.sel.why: From the model's questions; see the rationale on each card.
fields.cp[0].s0: Assess the curricular variables associated with the behavior: difficulty relative to current skills, task length, functional versus arbitrary tasks, preference, novelty.
fields.cp[0].s1: Assess the instructional variables: session length, massed versus interspersed trials, prompting method, trial rate, density of positive reinforcement during work.
fields.cp[0].s2: Revise: teach prerequisite skills before advanced ones; shorten sessions; intersperse easy and mastered tasks; use the prompting method the student tolerates.
fields.cp[0].s3: Increase positive reinforcement for compliance and task completion during instruction (denser than any break contingency).
fields.cp[0].s4: Re-evaluate the behavior under the revised curriculum before adding consequence-based components.
fields.cp[1].s0: Identify high-p and low-p instructions from caregiver and staff nominations, then test each on 10 probe trials in random order: high-p = cooperation on at least 80% of trials, low-p = under 40% (the operational definitions of Lemons & Wilder, 2026); build a pool of at least six single-step, brief high-p instructions on the Antecedents sheet planner.
fields.cp[1].s1: Deliver 3 high-p instructions 1–3 s apart (the next immediately after cooperation) with brief praise for each; deliver the low-p instruction within 3 s of cooperation with the third, and only after cooperation with all three (study values, not tested optima).
fields.cp[1].s2: Order: varied (a different order each trial, never the previous trial's order) unless a brief probe preassessment shows a constant order is equal or better (Lemons & Wilder, 2026 recommendation); if constant, write the fixed order.
fields.cp[1].s3: If a high-p instruction is not cooperated with: pause 30 s and restart a new 3-instruction sequence; do not deliver the low-p instruction. Score cooperation as initiation within 10 s.
fields.cp[1].s4: Reinforce low-p cooperation per the plan (praise in the study; the authors suggest higher-quality reinforcement in practice); the consequence for low-p noncooperation comes from the Responding sheet by function; fade the number of high-p requests as cooperation holds.
fields.cp[2].s0: Intersperse mastered, easy items among difficult ones (e.g., 3 easy : 1 hard) during instruction.
fields.cp[2].s1: Praise each correct easy item; keep the pace brisk.
fields.cp[2].s2: Adjust the ratio from the behavior data; reduce interspersal as tolerance grows.
fields.cp[3].s0: Present instruction at a brisk pace with short response intervals; avoid long waits between items.
fields.cp[3].s1: Keep work periods short (e.g., 5 min) with a scheduled break, lengthening as the behavior stays low.
fields.cp[3].s2: Use the student's preferred and functional tasks where the curriculum allows.
fields.cp[4].s0: Prepare 3–4 task sets at the student's instructional level.
fields.cp[4].s1: Before each work period present the array and let the student choose the order (or the timing) of tasks.
fields.cp[4].s2: When one task is complete, offer the remaining tasks again.
fields.cp[4].s3: Pair with a consequence component (extinction or DNRA) because choice alone programs no consequence for problem behavior.
fields.cp[4].s4: Record choice made, task completed, and problem behavior per period.
fields.cp[5].s0: Provide a visual or picture activity schedule the student manipulates (check off, move a card) as each activity ends.
fields.cp[5].s1: Give an advance notice before transitions (e.g., 2-min and 30-s warnings) and a consistent transition signal.
fields.cp[5].s2: Preview any change to the routine at the start of the day; keep the order stable where possible.
fields.cp[5].s3: For transition-evoked behavior, combine with the function-based component identified on EA-1 (Wilder et al., 2006).
fields.cp[6].s0: Preview the next day's or next period's materials in a low-demand, preferred context (with a parent or aide) before the lesson.
fields.cp[6].s1: Keep priming brief and reinforcing; do not test.
fields.cp[6].s2: Track performance and problem behavior in the primed lessons versus unprimed ones.
fields.cp[7].s0: At arrival, check the setting events the assessment identified (sleep, illness, allergy symptoms, missed medication, conflict on the bus or at home, hunger) with the parent note or a brief check.
fields.cp[7].s1: When a setting event is present, run the neutralizing routine: a preferred activity first, reduced or shortened demands, extra noncontingent attention, and choice for that morning (Horner et al., 1997).
fields.cp[7].s2: Record the setting event and the routine used on the data sheet; report medical setting events to the nurse.
fields.cp[8].s0: Identify the specific social consequence the student prefers (form of praise, tickles, conversation, high five) with a social-interaction preference assessment (Smaby et al., 2007; Call et al., 2013).
fields.cp[8].s1: Deliver it immediately and enthusiastically for the target response; keep it brief.
fields.cp[8].s2: Test it under intermittent schedules before relying on it; if it weakens, back it with tangibles or tokens.
fields.cp[9].s0: Completing a unit schedule (e.g., FR 3 correct) earns a token; completing the exchange schedule (e.g., 5 tokens) earns the backup reinforcer.
fields.cp[9].s1: Establish tokens by pairing with immediate exchange at first (exchange after 1 token), then lengthen the exchange requirement.
fields.cp[9].s2: Offer a menu of backup reinforcers to limit satiation; keep the exchange schedule dense enough to contact the backup daily.
fields.cp[9].s3: Thin the unit schedule before the exchange schedule.
fields.cp[10].s0: Line up 5–7 items; the student approaches one and receives brief access; remove it and re-present the rest until all are chosen or 30 s passes without a choice.
fields.cp[10].s1: Repeat 3–5 times; rank by mean selection order or percentage.
fields.cp[10].s2: Use the brief version before sessions to track daily shifts (DeLeon et al., 2001).
fields.cp[11].s0: Reinforce every occurrence of the target response during acquisition.
fields.cp[11].s1: Hold CRF until the response is independent and stable.
fields.cp[11].s2: Thin only by a planned schedule (see the thinning ladder).
fields.cp[12].s0: Begin with the prompt that guarantees the response (e.g., full physical), delivered immediately with the instruction.
fields.cp[12].s1: Reduce to the next less intrusive level after the criterion (e.g., 3 consecutive correct); return one level after 2 errors.
fields.cp[12].s2: Reinforce prompted responses during acquisition; differentially reinforce unprompted responses once they appear.
fields.cp[12].s3: Use when errors evoke problem behavior or the response is new.
fields.cp[13].s0: Begin with a 0-s delay between instruction and prompt; increase the delay in small steps (e.g., 1 s per session or per criterion) as unprompted responses appear.
fields.cp[13].s1: Transfer of control is shown when the learner responds before the prompt; keep the terminal delay short enough to prevent errors.
fields.cp[13].s2: Reinforce unprompted responses more richly than prompted ones.
fields.cp[14].s0: In every teaching trial deliver the instruction and the controlling prompt together (0-s delay).
fields.cp[14].s1: Run daily probe trials without the prompt to measure acquisition; probes are the only unprompted opportunities.
fields.cp[14].s2: Use when errors must be near zero and probes can be scheduled.
fields.cp[15].s0: Compare candidate prompt types (vocal, model, physical) or hierarchies (MTL vs LTM) on equivalent skill sets in an alternating-treatments design.
fields.cp[15].s1: Select the procedure that produced the fastest acquisition with the fewest errors and least problem behavior.
fields.cp[15].s2: Re-run when a new response class is introduced.
fields.cp[16].s0: After an error, model or deliver the correct response, then re-present the instruction and require an independent (or least-prompted) correct response before moving on.
fields.cp[16].s1: Reinforce the corrected response with praise only; reserve the token or item for unprompted responses.
fields.cp[17].s0: After the tolerance response, present one contextually appropriate behavior (relinquish the item, transition, or complete one instruction) before the synthesized reinforcers are delivered.
fields.cp[17].s1: Lengthen the chain and vary its content unpredictably (one instruction → three → a short task → a full routine) while keeping some trials in which the FCR is honored immediately.
fields.cp[17].s2: Reinforce the chain with the synthesized reinforcers at a decreasing but unpredictable probability; add praise throughout.
fields.cp[17].s3: Extend to new implementers and settings with the same sequence; probe the natural routine before and after.
fields.cp[18].s0: Assess the current mand: does it occur only after a vocal prompt or the item in view (prompt or stimulus control) or under the EO alone?
fields.cp[18].s1: Fade the prompt and the visible item with a time delay so the mand occurs in the absence of both.
fields.cp[18].s2: For sign or picture mands, pair the vocal model and reinforce vocal approximations to move toward vocal mands (Carbone et al., 2010).
fields.cp[19].s0: Capture naturally occurring EOs during routines (snack, play, transitions); pause and wait for the mand before providing the item or action.
fields.cp[19].s1: Prompt only as needed, fade quickly, and reinforce with the item requested.
fields.cp[19].s2: Rotate across settings, listeners, and items to build generalized manding; record mands per hour in the natural routine.
fields.cp[20].s0: Before the activity, have the student state what they will do ("I will use the break card if the work is hard"); reinforce the statement at first (reinforce-saying phase).
fields.cp[20].s1: Shift reinforcement to correspondence: reinforce only when the stated behavior occurs (reinforce-correspondence phase); use say-then-do ordering (Israel & O'Leary, 1973).
fields.cp[20].s2: Fade to intermittent checks and to the student's own review of correspondence.
fields.cp[20].s3: Use when the student can state a plan and the goal is self-management across settings.
fields.cp[21].s0: Score the relevant modules (basic living, home, community participation, school, vocational, independent living).
fields.cp[21].s1: Select functional skills the replacement behavior will make possible (e.g., requesting help during a chore).
fields.cp[21].s2: Teach with the prompting and error-correction procedures chosen on the prompting sheet; track independence per skill.
fields.cp[22].p0: Block the hit with an open hand or a folder; keep the task in view; say nothing about the hit; after 10 s re-present the demand (escape extinction, consented); prompt the card at the next demand.
fields.cp[22].p2: If hitting continues for 2 minutes or a peer is struck twice, follow CR-1 (clear peers, call the second adult); no restraint; nurse check for any mark.
fields.cp[22].s0: On the precursor: At the first push-away or "I'm done": prompt the break card (hand over hand if needed), honor it at once, say "Break" and remove the task for 2 minutes.
fields.cp[22].s1: On the target behavior: Block the hit with an open hand or a folder; keep the task in view; say nothing about the hit; after 10 s re-present the demand (escape extinction, consented); prompt the card at the next demand.
fields.cp[22].s2: After the episode: Resume the work period at the same task; no discussion of the hit; record the episode on DD-1 with the antecedent.
fields.cp[22].s3: Staff do not: Do not remove the task after a hit; do not send to the hall or office; do not reprimand or lecture; do not add work as a consequence.
fields.cp[22].s4: Record the episode, the step used, and whether the reinforcer was contacted (integrity error).
fields.cp[22].s5: Crisis procedure applies only when the safety trigger is met and is documented separately.
fields.cp[23].bsrc: Work-then-ask play break (FCT with a growing work requirement) for escape-maintained destructive behavior (Harding et al., 2009)
fields.cp[23].p0: say 'play', sign it, or gently touch a 'play' picture card mounted on a single-message switch that speaks 'play, please'; other polite ways of saying finished (e.g., 'done') were also honored
fields.cp[23].p1: adult models the task before the student does it; at first the adult tells the student to say 'play' or touch the switch, and this cue is faded as independent requests appear; hand-over-hand help for the task only when needed
fields.cp[23].p2: 1-minute break in the play area with preferred toys and adult attention, plus praise for finished work
fields.cp[23].p3: problem behavior never ends the work: the adult briefly names the behavior, presents another task and requires it before the next chance to ask; refusing to ask also leads to another task; a break is ended early if destructive behavior occurs during it
fields.cp[23].p4: raise the work required before each chance to ask while keeping two break chances per 5-minute session: 1 task per trial (2 per session), then 2 per trial (4 per session), then 4 per trial (8 per session)
fields.cp[23].p5: chance to ask for a 1-minute break after 4 completed tasks (8 tasks per 5-minute session)
fields.cp[23].s0: Set up a work area (small desk and chair) separate from a play area that holds the student's preferred toys.
fields.cp[23].s1: Begin each 5-minute session with a few minutes of play with the preferred toys and your full attention.
fields.cp[23].s2: Show the work picture card, tell the student it is time to work at the desk, and guide the student to the seat in small steps, praising each step.
fields.cp[23].s3: Model one easy task (for example, stacking one block), then have the student do it and praise independent completion.
fields.cp[23].s4: After the required number of tasks, present the play card on the switch and offer a choice of more work or play, cueing the student to say 'play' or touch the switch until that cue can be faded.
fields.cp[23].s5: When the student asks appropriately (says 'play', signs, touches the switch gently, or says 'done'), remove the work card and materials and give a 1-minute play break with toys and attention.
fields.cp[23].s6: If the student refuses to ask, asks roughly (hits the switch, yells), or shows problem behavior, give no break: briefly correct or name the behavior, present another task, and require it before the next chance to ask.
fields.cp[23].s7: If destructive behavior occurs during a break, end the break and return the student to the desk for another task.
fields.cp[23].s8: As the student succeeds, raise the work before each chance to ask from 1 to 2 to 4 tasks per trial (2, 4, then 8 tasks per session), keeping two break chances per session.
fields.cp[23].s9: Once performance is stable, probe and then extend the same routine to new tasks, people and settings.
fields.cp[23].data: Percentage of 6-s intervals with destructive behavior (aggression, self-injury, property destruction) and with independent requests for play, plus each task coded as done independently, done with physical help, or not done, per 5-minute session, recorded on Form DD-1.
fields.cp[23].mat: Small desk and chair (work area); play area with preferred toys (an electronic game was the top item); 'work' picture card; 'play' picture card on a single-message voice-output switch; simple task materials such as stacking blocks; timer for the 1-minute break.
fields.cp[24].bsrc: Functional communication training with extinction and gradual, signaled schedule thinning (practice guide) (Tiger et al., 2008)
fields.cp[24].p0: a low-effort response that unfamiliar people will recognize and the student can learn fast, such as a picture exchange, a single sign, a voice-output button or a short vocal request; an existing response such as signing 'all done' can be strengthened; make it more complex once problem behavior is low
fields.cp[24].p1: most-to-least (physical prompt as soon as the motivating situation is set up, then faded in intensity) or least-to-most with a delay (wait about 5 s, then a vocal or physical prompt, with the delay lengthened over trials)
fields.cp[24].p2: the reinforcer found in the functional analysis, given every time at first; if extinction cannot be used, make reinforcement for the communication longer, better, faster or more frequent than for problem behavior
fields.cp[24].p3: withhold the maintaining reinforcer after problem behavior from the start of treatment
fields.cp[24].p4: lengthen a delay to reinforcement starting at 1 s with a signal that it is coming; or alternate signaled periods when requests are and are not honored (for example two colored cards); for escape, raise the amount of work required before a break request is honored
fields.cp[24].p5: a schedule caregivers can keep up; the guide cites success with requests honored only during signaled periods covering about 20% of the time
fields.cp[24].s0: Confirm the maintaining reinforcer with a functional analysis before starting.
fields.cp[24].s1: Pick a communication response that is low effort, easy for unfamiliar people to recognize, and quick to learn.
fields.cp[24].s2: Begin with a trained interventionist in a safe, controlled setting and create many practice opportunities by setting up the motivating situation (remove the item, withhold attention, or present the task).
fields.cp[24].s3: Prompt the communication response either right away (most-to-least) or after a short wait such as 5 s (least-to-most with a delay), and fade the prompt over trials.
fields.cp[24].s4: Deliver the maintaining reinforcer every time the student communicates during initial training.
fields.cp[24].s5: Withhold the maintaining reinforcer after problem behavior.
fields.cp[24].s6: Once problem behavior is low, thin reinforcement gradually using a signaled delay starting at 1 s, signaled periods when requests can and cannot be honored, or, for escape, more work before the break request is honored.
fields.cp[24].s7: Offer other preferred items during delays or unavailable periods to compete with problem behavior during thinning.
fields.cp[24].s8: Extend training across several trainers and settings, bring in materials from the classroom, train in each needed setting, and teach caregivers how to respond.
fields.cp[24].s9: Increase the complexity of the communication response over time, for example a full request such as 'May I have ___, please'.
fields.cp[24].data: Rate of problem behavior and of independent communication responses per session, prompt level used, and the current thinning step, plus probes in each setting and with each caregiver, recorded on Form DD-1.
fields.cp[24].mat: Communication materials (picture cards, voice-output device or sign), the reinforcer identified in the functional analysis, signals for reinforcement availability such as colored cards, a timer, and a protected setting for early training.
fields.ant.chosen: A_HIGHP, A_INTERSPERSE, A_PACE, CHOICE, A_SCHEDULE, A_PRIME, A_SETEVENT
fields.ec.0: no, the prompting procedure is errorless
fields.skb.1: contrived sessions first, then natural routines
fields.rb.prec: At the first push-away or "I'm done": prompt the break card (hand over hand if needed), honor it at once, say "Break" and remove the task for 2 minutes.
fields.rb.target: Block the hit with an open hand or a folder; keep the task in view; say nothing about the hit; after 10 s re-present the demand (escape extinction, consented); prompt the card at the next demand.
fields.rb.after: Resume the work period at the same task; no discussion of the hit; record the episode on DD-1 with the antecedent.
fields.rb.not: Do not remove the task after a hit; do not send to the hall or office; do not reprimand or lecture; do not add work as a consequence.
fields.rb.crisis: If hitting continues for 2 minutes or a peer is struck twice, follow CR-1 (clear peers, call the second adult); no restraint; nurse check for any mark.
fields.p.visit: Weekly 30-minute visit: observe one session, score the integrity checklist, give feedback, model any step under 80%.
fields.p.pre: Probes before the plan starts: the target and the replacement behavior in 3 settings (class, specials, cafeteria) with 2 adults.
fields.p.gen: Train with two adults and in two settings from the first week; the natural cue (the demand itself) is the SD; the card goes with the student.
fields.p.post: Probes in the untrained setting at 2 and 4 weeks after criterion; monthly after.
fields.p.complex: The simple response first; the longer form once the simple one is at criterion.
fields.p.design: Baseline to treatment with the EA-1 treatment sheet; reversal only if the team agrees.
